title: Your first scene
subtitle: From an empty canvas to something real.

lessons.title: Hello, third dimension
body: Welcome to your little 3D studio. A scene holds objects, a camera chooses the view, and a renderer draws that view onto a canvas. Three.js connects these pieces to the browser’s graphics system.

The workspace has already created scene, camera, renderer, and orbit controls for you. The code below builds the cube and its lighting. Start small: change the background color and watch the viewer update. Drag the viewer to look around; scroll to zoom.
lessons.task: Change the scene background from #10141f to #242038.
lessons.hint: Edit the color string on the first line. Quotes and the # are part of the value.

quiz.question: Which part decides what appears in the final image?
quiz.explanation: The camera defines the viewpoint. The renderer draws the scene from that viewpoint.

lessons.title: A shape needs a surface
body: Geometry describes an object’s shape. A material describes how its surface looks. A Mesh combines both into an object you can position in a scene.
Built-in geometries are a quick way to experiment. BoxGeometry takes width, height, and depth. SphereGeometry starts with a radius. Swapping geometry keeps the material and lighting intact.
lessons.task: Replace the box geometry with new THREE.SphereGeometry(1, 32, 24).
lessons.hint: Keep the variable name geometry. Only replace the constructor and its arguments.

quiz.question: What does a material describe?
quiz.explanation: A material controls surface properties such as color, roughness, and transparency.

lessons.title: Give it a place in the scene
body: Creating a mesh does not automatically display it. Objects become renderable when they belong to the scene’s hierarchy, also called the scene graph.
This cube exists in memory, but its scene.add line is commented out. Restore the connection and it appears. Later, groups will let us organize related objects beneath a shared parent.
lessons.task: Uncomment scene.add(mesh) so the cube appears.
lessons.hint: Remove the two slashes before scene.add(mesh).

quiz.question: Why can a newly created mesh be invisible?
options: It has not been added to the scene
quiz.explanation: Constructing an object and adding it to the scene are separate operations.

lessons.title: Find your angle
lessons.concept: The camera is an object, too
body: A camera has a position in 3D space. Here, positive Y is up, and the cube sits near the origin: (0, 0, 0). Our orbit controls keep the view aimed at their target.
Move the camera higher by changing the middle coordinate. The cube stays in place; only your viewpoint changes. This is the same distinction as moving a real camera around a stationary subject.
lessons.hint: Change camera.position.set(4, 3, 6) near the top to camera.position.set(4, 6, 6).

quiz.question: Which coordinate is up in this workspace?
quiz.explanation: The workspace uses Three.js’s default Y-up convention.

lessons.title: Bring the cube to life
body: Animation is a sequence of slightly different images. Our workspace calls each onFrame callback before drawing the next image. Outside this workspace, you can set up that loop with renderer.setAnimationLoop.
The delta value is the number of seconds since the previous frame. Multiplying a speed by delta makes the rotation advance by time, even when different screens draw at different frame rates.
lessons.task: Set speed to 0.6 radians per second.
lessons.hint: Change const speed = 0 to const speed = 0.6.

quiz.question: Why multiply speed by delta?
options: To make motion depend on elapsed time
quiz.explanation: Time-based movement stays approximately consistent across different frame rates.
